title: Red night mode still paints the accent-colour swatches in full-saturation cyan, green and magenta
what_happened: Settings > Appearance under Theme = Red night shows the 7 accent swatches at their literal colours: sampled (16,185,129) green, (245,158,11) amber, (6,182,212) cyan, (236,72,153) magenta. On the same page every other pixel is red-shifted.
expected: Either suppress the swatch row in red night (the accent has no visible effect in a monochrome red theme anyway), or dim/annotate it. As shipped, opening Appearance at the telescope to check the theme is the thing that ruins your dark adaptation.
repro: Settings > Appearance > Theme > Red night; the Accent color row is directly under Theme.
proposed_fix: Hide or grey the accent row when theme == redNight, or render each swatch as a red-luminance equivalent with a small label.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and measured. With theme=redNight the Appearance page background is RGB(20,8,8) but the 7 accent swatches sample at their literal values along the row y=442: (91,158,196) blue, (16,185,129) green, (245,158,11) amber, (239,68,68) red, (40,120,168) steel, (236,72,153) magenta, (6,182,212) cyan. Identical to the reported samples. appearance_settings.dart:73-77 is the 'Accent color' SettingRow that hosts the swatch row, so the 'where' is right. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/19-rn.png.

title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima — a single tree blocks a whole 45-degree sector
what_happened: I imported a 36-point .hor file (one sample every 10 deg of azimuth, altitudes 10-29 deg). The snackbar said 'Horizon profile imported from test36.hor' and the eight compass fields filled in as N=25, NE=16, E=21, SE=25, S=29, SW=14, W=19, NW=23. Those are exactly the MAXIMUM sample in each 45 deg sector — the other 28 samples were discarded with no mention. Source confirms this is deliberate (location_settings.dart:498-501, 'highest altitude per sector wins'), but nothing in the UI says so.
expected: Real horizon files from Stellarium/HorizonBox have 1-degree resolution and are the reason people generate them. Max-per-sector means one 29-degree tree at azimuth 190 marks everything from 157.5 to 202.5 as blocked, so the planner and Tonight will refuse targets that are actually clear — this costs imaging time on exactly the targets a southern-horizon site cares about. At minimum the import must say 'imported 36 samples, reduced to 8 sectors (worst case per sector)'. Better: store the full profile and interpolate.
repro: Create a .hor with one line per 10 deg azimuth; Settings > Location > Local Horizon Mask > Import .hor / CSV; compare the eight resulting fields with the file.
evidence: Input /tmp/ns-audit/rsg-files/test36.hor; resulting horizon_profile_json from sqlite3: {"N":25.0,"NE":16.0,"E":21.0,"SE":25.0,"S":29.0,"SW":14.0,"W":19.0,"NW":23.0} — verified by hand to be the per-sector maxima. Snackbar text captured from tree.
proposed_fix: Persist the full sampled profile and interpolate at query time; keep the 8 fields as a coarse editor/summary. Failing that, report the sample count and the reduction in the success message.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed in source, which is decisive here. HorizonProfile.parseHorizonText (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_provider.dart:567-603) parses every sample, then hands them to HorizonProfile.fromSamples (:539-555), which rounds each azimuth to one of 8 45-degree sectors (index = floor(((az+22.5)%360)/45)%8) and keeps only 'if (alt > altitudes[dir]) altitudes[dir] = alt' — the per-sector MAXIMUM, discarding every other sample. location_settings.dart:497-501 documents the reduction ('highest altitude per sector wins so an obstruction is never under-reported') and :526 shows the only user-facing message: 'Horizon profile imported from <file>' — no sample count, no mention of the reduction. Severity lowered to P3 because the app's horizon model is 8-sector everywhere (horizonDirections), so the reduction is intrinsic and conservative; the shippable defect is the silence about it, not a wrong number. Did not drive the native file-picker; the source path is unambiguous and the reported 8 values are consistent with per-sector maxima.

title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, a location the Files & Storage page never names and offers no way to change
what_happened: 'Enable automatic backups' defaults ON with a 24 h interval and 'Maximum backups 7'. The page shows File Paths for 'Image output' and 'Sequences' and says application data is 'Managed automatically in Skotiq's application data folder' — but it never says where backups go. They go to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups, i.e. ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely: this sandboxed audit instance, whose data dir is /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data, wrote its backups into the real user's Documents folder. 'Maximum backups' then PRUNES files in that undisclosed directory.
expected: The Status section should show the backup folder path with a 'Reveal' action and let the user change it (backups belong on the same drive the user actually backs up, and an observatory PC's Documents folder is often the smallest volume). Retention that deletes files must name the folder it deletes from. Honouring the configured data directory is the minimum.
repro: Fresh profile with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data. Wait 5 min or press Back Up Now. `find /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general -iname '*backup*'` -> nothing; `ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups` -> skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-45.572326.nsbackup and two more from this run.
evidence: backup_service.dart:1025-1030 `_getBackupDirectory` = getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups with no settings override wired up; observed files listed above; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/07-files-scroll.png shows the Status card with no path.
proposed_fix: Add a 'Backup folder' path row to Files & Storage (browse + reveal), default it under the app data dir, and show the resolved path in the Status card.
verdict_reasoning: HALF of this is already fixed and must not be re-fixed. The path half is FIXED: backup_service.dart:1051-1055 _getBackupDirectory now calls the new resolveDefaultBackupDirectory() (:135-145), which resolves 'backups/' beside resolveDefaultDatabaseFile(environment) and therefore honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR. Verified live: this sandboxed instance wrote /tmp/ns-audit/v2-settings-general/data/backups/skotiq_autosave_2026-08-03T16-44-36.898434.nsbackup, and 'find ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups -newermt 2026-08-03' returns nothing. The disclosure half still reproduces: AutoSaveConfig defaults are backupEnabled=true, backupInterval=24h, maxBackups=7 (auto_save_service.dart:26-33), and the Status section (auto_save_settings.dart:306-372) renders only 'Last backup', 'Last error' and a 'Back Up Now' button — it never names the directory and offers no way to change it, while 'Maximum backups' prunes files in that unnamed folder. Severity dropped to P3 now that the cross-install/undeclared-volume leak is gone.
